source.title: Language Models "Grok" to Copy
source.authors: Ang Lv; Ruo-Bing Xie; Xing-Wu Sun; Zhan-Hui Kang; Rui Yan

record.tranche_reason: Measures context-copying performance over pretraining and measures induction-head scores, but uses a different setup and outcome than a direct replication of the original claim.
record.gate_note: The study reports context-copying accuracy, training loss, an ICL score, and induction-score dynamics. It also reports changes under batch size, learning rate, dropout, and weight decay. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study pretrains 162M 12-layer Llama models on RedPajama and tracks three things across checkpoints: random-token context-copying accuracy (an induction-style [A][B]…[A]→[B] task), Olsson's ICL score, and a per-head induction score. It also varies batch size, learning rate, dropout and weight decay. These are its own results on when and how induction behaviour forms, so they bear on V2, V4, V5 and V7. It does not causally test composition (V1). It does not evaluate few-shot ICL tasks (V3, V6).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors argue that context copying develops like grokking. Copying accuracy on random-token sequences surges at 15B tokens, long after loss stabilizes at 5B and after the ICL score saturates at ~4k steps. Onset depends on update steps, not tokens, and comes earlier with a higher learning rate. Induction heads form from shallow to deep layers. Dropout accelerates copying, and both dropout and weight decay improve final accuracy. They note they did not evaluate ICL tasks.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates random-token context copying during pretraining and measures induction scores across checkpoints, rather than reproducing the original study's full induction-head and in-context-learning analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: Copying development varies with batch size, learning rate, attention dropout, and weight decay; larger batch sizes slow copying in token-count terms, and higher learning rates accelerate and strengthen copying.
record.peer_reviewed: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The authors did not evaluate ICL tasks, citing limited computational resources. Induction-score evolution is shown for a single model. Several plotted results have no numeric values in the text, and uncertainty estimates are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No reported results relevant to the claim were left out.

untested.parts: Composition with a previous-token head is described from the literature, not tested. No attention-only models and no causal analysis.
Timing of induction-score onset relative to ICL-score gain and loss is shown only in a figure. The loss bump is not examined.
Not tested. The authors did not evaluate ICL tasks.
Only one architecture at one size (162M Llama). Induction scores are shown for a single model. No other families or modalities.
Training-data properties are not varied. Persistence of ICL is not tested. Hyperparameter effects are measured on copying accuracy, not on induction-head scores.
No quantitative timing of the per-layer sub-steps is given. Whether these are distinct or overlapping transitions is not analysed.

missing.what: With fixed learning rate, training-loss convergence tracks token count while copying accuracy tracks update steps and is slower with larger batches
Per-layer induction-score values and the timing of their rise relative to the ICL-score saturation and the copying surge

record.verdict_notes: I removed V1 from r7: no composition test, and the model is not attention-only. I relabelled r2 and r3 as cannot_determine rather than absent, because the text simply does not report a bump or abruptness. I changed the V2 verdict from challenges to limits_scope: the early ICL-score saturation is consistent with V2, and only the harder long-range copying ability arrives late. Hyperparameter rows measure copying accuracy, not induction scores. The General Setup lists LR 0.1, which conflicts with Figure 5 and is likely a typo. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Seed averaging (3 seeds) applies to accuracy, not to Figure 6.

versions.untested_parts: Does not causally test composition with an earlier previous-token head, or test the mechanism in attention-only transformers.

Does not establish the timing of induction-head formation relative to the ICL score and loss curve; it measures copying dynamics and reports induction-score evolution, but does not report an induction-head onset coincident with an ICL gain or a loss bump.
The authors state that they did not evaluate ICL tasks or robust ICL performance.
Does not compare model families, substantially different model sizes, other architectures, or modalities.
Varies training batch size, learning rate, dropout, and weight decay, but does not vary data properties or test whether ICL persists.
Does not test few-shot task learning or compare its mechanisms with copying.
Does not resolve whether the shallow-to-deep pattern consists of distinct sub-steps or overlapping transitions.

rows.subject: 12-layer Llama model (162M parameters), batch size 64
rows.operation_detail: Measured context-copying accuracy across training checkpoints.

conditions.value: copying accuracy low until 10B tokens; surge at 15B tokens

rows.baseline: Accuracy is reported as low until 10B tokens.
rows.value: A surge in accuracy occurs at 15B tokens.
rows.note: The text describes a sharp increase in copying accuracy, but does not give the accuracy values.
rows.check: Copying accuracy does jump abruptly, but late: 'low until 10B tokens', surge at 15B (~38k steps). That is long after loss stabilizes (5B) and the ICL score saturates (~4k steps, 1.85B tokens). No coincident loss bump is reported. So the abrupt-gain part holds but the early-window part does not. The task is a long-range multi-token copy (12-gram prefix, 6-gram suffix, 50 sequences), harder than the original's repeated-token measure.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V2. Long-range copying accuracy surges at 15B tokens, but this does not establish when induction heads first appear or their coincidence with an ICL-score gain.
source_check.locator_found: Section 3, Figure 2 and accompanying paragraph; Section 5, discussion point 2.
source_check.problem: Late mastery of the copying task is treated as late induction-head formation without establishing that correspondence.

rows.subject: 12-layer Llama model (162M parameters), batch size 64
rows.operation_detail: Tracked pretraining loss across training checkpoints.
rows.note: The reported trajectory is rapid decrease followed by stabilization; the text does not report a loss bump at the copying surge.
rows.check: The text only says loss 'stabilizes after 5B tokens'. It neither reports nor rules out a small bump near the early ICL-score transition (~1.85B tokens). The coarse token axis of Figure 2 cannot show the absence of a bump, so 'absent' overstates what is reported.

rows.subject: 12-layer Llama model (162M parameters), ICL-score measurement
rows.operation_detail: Measured the ICL score described as tracking in-context abilities.
rows.value: Stabilizes at -0.5 nats after approximately 4,000 steps.
rows.note: The authors contrast this stabilization with copying accuracy continuing to improve and surging later.
rows.check: The text gives only the saturation point (-0.5 nats after ~4,000 steps / 1.85B tokens). Early saturation is consistent with V2's early window, but abruptness and timing relative to induction-head formation are not reported. The row is not evidence of absence.

rows.subject: 12-layer Llama model (162M parameters), batch size 32
rows.operation_detail: Measured copying development in a batch-size training run.
rows.value: Fundamental copying ability develops after around 38,000 update steps.
rows.note: The authors report similar development by update step across the three batch sizes despite differing token counts.
rows.check: Batch size is per GPU (8 GPUs). The dependence shown is collective across r4–r6: onset is fixed in update steps (~38k), so token count at onset scales with batch size. The measure is copying accuracy, not induction-head score.

rows.operation_detail: Measured induction score for attention heads across layers during training.

rows.value: Induction heads develop from shallower to deeper layers during training.
rows.note: The figure shows per-head scores, but the text gives only the overall shallow-to-deep development pattern; no score values or exact transition times are stated.
rows.check: Drop V1. The induction score combines attention pattern and OV eigenvalue positivity and does not test composition with a previous-token head; the model is also not attention-only. relation.reason: Its own experiments bear on induction behaviour, progressive head development and training dependence.

tranche.reason: The study examines copying development, induction-head scores and training dependence using different measurements and a Llama pretraining setup.

source_check.notes: Figure 6 reports one model; copying accuracy is averaged over three seeds unless specified. The setup states learning rate 0.1, whereas Figure 5 explicitly labels 1e-4, 2e-4 and 4e-4; retain this source discrepancy.

statements.correction: Copying accuracy low until 10B tokens; surge at 15B; training loss stabilizes after 5B; ICL score stabilizes at -0.5 nats after approximately 4,000 steps, about 1.85B tokens; no reported loss bump; coincidence with induction-head onset undetermined.
statements.problem: The reported measurements are correct, but the limits_scope reading substitutes late long-range copying mastery for late induction-head formation. Their timing correspondence is not established.

statements.correction: 162M Llama copying accuracy low until 10B tokens and surging at 15B; ICL-score stabilization around 1.85B tokens; copying timing depends on training configuration; head-onset timing relative to these measurements not established.
statements.problem: The copying measurements and configuration dependence are correct. Treating this study as a V2 scope limitation requires an unestablished correspondence between copying-task mastery and induction-head onset.

statements.correction: Late random-token copying surge in 162M Llama; early ICL-score stabilization; timing of induction-head onset relative to the ICL transition undetermined; loss bump untested.
statements.problem: This study establishes late copying-task mastery, but does not establish that induction heads form late or fail to coincide with the early ICL-score transition.

statements.correction: Section 3 defines induction score I(L,H); Figure 6 tracks induction scores across checkpoints of a single model; batch-size, learning-rate and regularization comparisons report copying accuracy rather than corresponding head-score comparisons.
statements.problem: The unqualified assertion that this study does not measure induction scores is false. Its hyperparameter comparisons measure copying, while a separate analysis measures induction scores.
